provenance: Compiled from organisation guideline indices and PubMed. Every record was checked against a primary source. Fields marked confidence:'unconfirmed_pmid' have a verified DOI/journal but an unverified PMID and MUST NOT be emitted as a [PMID:N] citation until resolved.
ingest_notes: A guideline is NOT a paper. Do not place these on the study-design tier ladder. They occupy a parallel channel keyed by 'authority', not by 'tier'.

Several of these ARE PubMed-indexed and will therefore already be entering the corpus as if they were primary studies. Ingesting this manifest must DEDUPE against the existing paper table by PMID and reclassify those rows as guidelines.
The single most valuable field here is 'superseded_by'. A superseded guideline cited as current is a clinical hazard, not a formatting defect.
'jurisdiction' matters: NICE/SDCEP/CGDent bind UK practice; AAE/ADA/AAOMS are US. A UK clinician given only US guidance has been given the wrong answer.

2026-09-06 extension: US specialty position statements (AAO, ACP, AAOM, AAOP, AAOMP, ASDA/ASA), the ADA 2025 sedation guidelines and the full IADT trauma lineage were added. Only HIGH/MEDIUM endodontic-relevance documents were seeded; every superseded predecessor with a PubMed accession was seeded too, because a superseded trauma or sedation guideline served as current is the hazard this manifest exists to prevent. Guidelines are still NOT on the tier ladder; a specialty's position is surfaced under 'Where the specialty stands' and, where two specialties disagree (e.g. ACP asymptomatic-extraction vs endodontic tooth preservation), BOTH are shown and labelled.

guidelines.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines for Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics

AAO says it is reviewed every two years; a 2025 revision could not be confirmed. The PDF is behind an AAO member login. Explicitly 'not put forth as standards of treatment'. Lists root resorption (options: monitor radiographically / extraction / stabilisation / rest periods) and tooth vitality as diagnostic considerations, and states the vitality of a tooth may be compromised by treatment. The AAO has NO separate position statement on root resorption, pulp vitality or CBCT that could be located on a primary source; a 2010 House resolution on CBCT is documented only in secondary literature and is deliberately not seeded.

CITATION TRAP: PMID 32633458 ('The ACP Parameters of Care', J Prosthodont 2020;29(5):367-368, DOI 10.1111/jopr.13198, Garcia LT) is a two-page EDITORIAL about the document, not the supplement - verified on PubMed 2026-09-06. guidelines.question: How should prosthodontic treatment be planned for patients on antiresorptive or antiangiogenic drugs, and what happens to unrestorable teeth?
guidelines.note: Approved 28 Feb 2016, reaffirmed 28 Feb 2021. States that teeth deemed unrestorable 'should be considered for endodontic therapy, coronectomy, and possible root cap placement' rather than extraction - consistent with AAOMS-MRONJ-2022, AAE-MRONJ-2026 and SDCEP-MRONJ-2017.

guidelines.title: Position Statement: Dental Implants
guidelines.question: Who should place dental implants, and when is an implant preferred over retaining a tooth?
guidelines.note: Approved 1 Oct 2014; revisions approved 9 Jun 2019. Implant placement is 'a procedure, not a specialty'; notes an endodontist may place an implant when a tooth cannot be successfully treated endodontically.

guidelines.title: Position Statement: Posterior Single Tooth Replacement
guidelines.question: How should a missing posterior single tooth be replaced - no treatment, removable partial denture, fixed partial denture or implant crown?
guidelines.note: Patient-centred choice; calls for prosthodontic, endodontic and periodontal input in planning.

guidelines.title: Position Statement: The Use of Dental Radiographs in Evaluation of Prosthetic Margins - Tooth-Supported Fixed Prostheses
guidelines.question: How should the marginal fit of tooth-supported fixed prostheses be evaluated, clinically and radiographically?
guidelines.note: Approved 28 Feb 2016; revised 8 Jun 2019. Combined clinical and radiographic assessment; declines to define an acceptable marginal gap.

guidelines.title: Position Statement: Diagnostic Imaging in the Treatment Planning, Surgical, and Prosthodontic Aspects of Implant Dentistry
guidelines.question: Which imaging - panoramic, intraoral or CBCT - is justified at each stage of implant treatment?
guidelines.note: Approved 28 Feb 2016, reaffirmed 24 Feb 2019. Panoramic/intraoral first; CBCT when clinically justified under ALARA; cites AAOMR, EAO, AO and ICOI guidance - consistent with AAE-AAOMR-CBCT-2025 and ADA-AAOMR-PATIENT-SELECTION-2026.

guidelines.title: AAOM Clinical Practice Statement: Subject: Dental Care for the Patient with an Oral Herpetic Lesion
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2016;121(6):623-625
guidelines.question: Should elective dental treatment be deferred in a patient with an active oral herpetic lesion, and how should emergency care be delivered?
guidelines.note: AAOM Clinical Practice Statements are short expert-consensus statements approved by the AAOM Executive Committee and co-published in OOOO from 2016 (series editorial PMID 24439914). Their stated review-due dates (2016-2017) have lapsed with no published revision and AAOM has issued no revision or retirement notices; no CPS after February 2019 exists.

guidelines.title: AAOM Clinical Practice Statement: Subject: Dental Evaluation Before Head and Neck Radiotherapy
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2016;122(5):564-565
guidelines.question: How should the dentition be assessed and treated before head and neck radiotherapy, and which teeth should be extracted rather than retained?
guidelines.note: Adopted 6 Oct 2014, revised 2 Feb 2015 (Peterson); AAOM web title adds 'With or Without Chemotherapy'. The endodontic-treatment-versus-extraction decision before radiotherapy is where this statement bites.

guidelines.title: AAOM Clinical Practice Statement: Subject: Management of Patients on Warfarin Therapy
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2016;122(6):702-704
guidelines.question: Should warfarin be altered before dental procedures, and up to what INR can invasive dental treatment proceed?
guidelines.note: Adopted 1 Oct 2014 (Lockhart), review due Oct 2016 - lapsed. Position: do not alter warfarin; moderately invasive surgery such as uncomplicated extraction is safe with an INR up to 3.5 using local haemostatic measures. SILENT ON DOACs (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban), which it predates - hence 'current_but_stale'. The fuller operative document for anticoagulant questions is SDCEP-ANTICOAGULANTS-2022 (UK jurisdiction); surface both and label them.

guidelines.title: AAOM clinical practice statement: Subject: The use of serum C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type 1 collagen (CTX) testing in predicting risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ)
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2017;124(4):367-368
guidelines.question: Should serum CTX be used to predict osteonecrosis-of-the-jaw risk before dental procedures in patients on antiresorptive drugs?
guidelines.note: Journal-only: NOT listed on the AAOM CPS web index, and no revision or retirement notice exists, so its endorsement status is unconfirmed. Read alongside AAOMS-MRONJ-2022, which addresses the same test.

guidelines.title: The American Academy of Oral Medicine Clinical Practice Statement: Somatic symptom and related disorders
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2017;124(5):472-474
guidelines.question: How should somatic symptom and related disorders presenting as oral or facial complaints be recognised, so that unwarranted dental and endodontic intervention is avoided?
guidelines.note: Indexed by PubMed as a Practice Guideline. Journal-only (not on the AAOM web index). Relevant to persistent pain after technically adequate endodontic treatment; pair with AAOP-GUIDELINES-2023.

guidelines.title: The American Academy of Oral Medicine clinical practice statement: dental care for the patient on antiresorptive drug therapy
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2019;127(2):136-139
guidelines.question: How should dental care, including the choice between endodontic treatment and extraction, be planned for patients on bisphosphonates or denosumab?
guidelines.note: Bugueno & Migliorati. The most recent AAOM position on antiresorptives; supersedes the 2005 bisphosphonate position paper in content. Journal-only (not on the AAOM web index). No PubMed accession could be found by title, author or DOI search on 2026-09-06 - it may be unindexed or indexed under a variant title; render by id. Full text not reviewed: the specific recommendations are NOT restated here.

guidelines.title: Managing the care of patients with bisphosphonate-associated osteonecrosis: an American Academy of Oral Medicine position paper
guidelines.question: (Historic) prevention and dental management of bisphosphonate-associated osteonecrosis in cancer and osteoporosis patients.
guidelines.note: Migliorati et al. Pre-'MRONJ' terminology and pre-denosumab. No formal AAOM withdrawal, but overtaken by AAOM-CPS-ANTIRESORPTIVE-2019 and, externally, AAOMS-MRONJ-2022. Status deliberately 'superseded_in_content', not 'superseded'.

guidelines.title: The dental treatment of patients with joint replacements: a position paper from the American Academy of Oral Medicine
guidelines.question: Is antibiotic prophylaxis warranted before dental procedures in patients with prosthetic joints?
guidelines.note: Little, Jacobson & Lockhart; indexed by PubMed as a Practice Guideline. Position: risks and costs do not justify routine prophylaxis. Not withdrawn, but predates the 2015 ADA clinical practice guideline on prosthetic joints (same conclusion) and ADA-ANTIBIOTIC-STEWARDSHIP-2026 - hence 'current_but_stale'.

guidelines.title: Orofacial Pain: Guidelines for Assessment, Diagnosis, and Management, Seventh Edition
guidelines.question: How should orofacial pain - including non-odontogenic toothache, neuropathic and persistent dentoalveolar pain, and TMD-referred pain - be assessed, classified and managed?
guidelines.note: A BOOK (Quintessence; eds Klasser & Romero-Reyes), not a journal article: the AAOP publishes its positions through it. ICD-11/ICOP-aligned. The 5th edition is catalogued by NLM as a Practice Guideline (NLM ID 101603146). The 6th edition (2018) is still widely cited and is SUPERSEDED; no 8th edition existed as of 2026-09-06. The AAOP's own 'Guidelines & Landmark Articles' page lists third-party documents (ICOP, DC/TMD, NASEM 2020) that are NOT AAOP statements.

guidelines.title: Recommendations for imaging of the temporomandibular joint. Position statement from the American Academy of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology and the American Academy of Orofacial Pain
guidelines.journal: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2022;134(5):639-648; co-published J Oral Facial Pain Headache 2023;37(1):7-15
guidelines.question: When and how should the temporomandibular joint be imaged - examination design, in-office CBCT, MRI - across TMJ conditions?
guidelines.note: Mallya et al. Borderline endodontic relevance: TMD is a differential for toothache and many endodontists own a CBCT, but TMJ imaging itself is rarely an endodontic task.

guidelines.title: The use of biopsy in dental practice. The position of the American Academy of Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology
guidelines.question: When should a lesion be biopsied in dental practice, and how should the specimen be taken and submitted?
guidelines.note: Melrose et al.; indexed by PubMed as a Practice Guideline. Biopsy as the diagnostic gold standard, within general dentists' scope; ten guidelines for a successful biopsy. Not on the current AAOMP position-paper index and never revised; no withdrawal found - hence 'current_but_stale'. Pair with AAOMP-EXCISED-TISSUE-2013 for the periapical specimen from endodontic microsurgery.

guidelines.title: Policy on Excised Tissue (Handling Biopsies)
guidelines.question: Must tissue removed during oral surgery, including periapical tissue from apical surgery, be submitted for histopathological examination?
guidelines.note: Position: ALL excised oral and maxillofacial tissue should be submitted for microscopic examination by a certified oral and maxillofacial pathologist, with narrow exemptions (e.g. clinically normal extracted teeth), documented with a written report. Directly governs the periapical specimen from endodontic microsurgery. File dated 11 Nov 2013; no adoption date printed in the text.

guidelines.title: Narrative review: bisphosphonates and osteonecrosis of the jaws
guidelines.question: (Historic) what was known about bisphosphonate-associated osteonecrosis, and how should dental surgery be approached in exposed patients?
guidelines.note: Woo, Hellstein & Kalmar. Published as 'Systematic review: ...'; PubMed later corrected the title to 'Narrative review'. Carries the note 'This is a position paper of the American Academy of Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology' and is still listed as current by AAOMP, but predates MRONJ terminology and denosumab and is clinically overtaken by AAOMS-MRONJ-2022 - hence 'current_but_stale'. Recommends eliminating jaw infection before bisphosphonate therapy and minimal bone manipulation. If this PMID is already in the paper table it will be RECLASSIFIED on ingest; the dry run will show it.

extension_log.verification: Every confidence:'confirmed' PMID added on this date was checked on pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (title, journal, volume/issue/pages, DOI). Records whose accession could not be established carry confidence:'unconfirmed_pmid' and pmid:null.
deliberately_excluded: AAPHD: zero records - every policy is public-health (fluoridation, access, workforce); nothing answers a clinical question.
AAO 2010 House resolution on CBCT: documented only in secondary literature, no primary source located - not seeded.
AAO teledentistry parameters, DTC position paper, AI position paper, sleep-disordered-breathing white papers (2019 PMID 31256826 -> 2026 PMID 41770191): LOW endodontic relevance.

ACP: 25+ administrative and LOW-relevance position statements (denture care, sleep apnoea, ectodermal dysplasia, zygomatic implants, etc.) and the 1999-2004 Prosthodontic Diagnostic Index classifications.
AAOM CPS with LOW relevance (medical history, risk assessment, oral cancer screening, contact allergy, xerostomia, lichen planus, medication-induced reactions, dystonia, leukoplakia).
AAOMP oral lichen planus 2016 (PMID 27401683) and diagnostic-aids 2008 (PMID 17825602): LOW relevance.
ASDA/AAOMS/AAP model state sedation rules 2023, ASA/SPA/ASDA/SPS paediatric single-operator statement 2019, ASDA COVID guidance, ASDA code of ethics: regulatory or LOW relevance.
ADA 2007 sedation guidelines, 2007 policy statement, 2021 paediatric teaching guideline: LOW relevance; the 2007 use guideline is recorded in the 2025 record's supersedes chain.
IADT/ASD prevention series Parts 2-10: recorded as PMIDs inside the Part 1 anchor record rather than ten rows.

known_defects_this_manifest_closes: The bare key '(ESE-QG-2023)' leaking into Literature citation slots resolves to ESE-QG-2006, which is SUPERSEDED — the leaked key was also wrong about the year.
The bare key '[PMID AAE-PS-diagnosis]' leaking into Case citation slots resolves to AAE-DIAGNOSIS-2009.

PMID 41121563 and PMID 40533920 are already in the corpus as papers. They are the AAPD permanent-teeth VPT guideline and its supporting review. Reclassifying them explains why a paediatric guideline anchored a mature-permanent-teeth curriculum at score 80.0.
EFCD-ESE-ORCA-DEEPCARIES-2026 (PMID 42018467) is the guideline the VPT curriculum missed entirely.

Three Cochrane reviews in the endodontic space are WITHDRAWN (CD007997, CD005408, CD004623). Cochrane sits at the top of the tier ladder; a withdrawn review cited as top-tier evidence is a clinical-safety defect.
